subject: Coordinating MAP + MSA/DPA/Order Form sequencing for Aurelia pilot
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureliahealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MAP / legal sequencing questions for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile on the sampling demo. We want to move the pilot into an evaluation period but need to lock down the procurement path so our SSO/security folks and legal know what to expect. A couple of quick asks from our side: 

- Can you share a recommended mutual action plan (MAP) that sequences the evaluation milestones alongside the MSA/DPA and order form? We need clear gates for data access, security review, and go/no-go signoffs.
- What are typical lead times your legal ops expects for DPA review + countersignature? We may need to route to our compliance office early.
- For the pilot, we plan to ingest PHI-limited de-identified logs into a private environment; can you confirm whether Redwood Private or Dedicated is recommended from a procurement/contracting standpoint?

I attached a short outline of our internal acceptance criteria. If you and your legal team can sketch a timeline (high level) for MSA -> DPA -> order form, that would help us align dates with our procurement sprint (targeting decisions by 12/20).

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Aurelia Health

Attachment: Aurelia_acceptance_criteria.pdf (pdf)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@aureliahealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MAP / legal sequencing questions for pilot

Marta — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the acceptance list. High level answers below and I attached a draft MAP that maps evaluation milestones to procurement/legal gates.

- Recommended sequencing (high level):
  1) Evaluation kickoff + baseline data access (non-PHI synthetic dataset)
  2) Security questionnaire + initial evidence (SOC2 summary + network diagram)
  3) MSA draft shared (commercial terms) concurrent with security review
  4) DPA redline cycle (privacy specifics) — usually 1–2 rounds
  5) Order form (pricing, reserved capacity if applicable) and signature
  6) Pilot production access (private/dedicated environment)

- Typical DPA lead time: 7–14 business days for counter-signature on average when negotiations are limited to standard clauses; longer if customers require heavy redlines or custom security obligations. We recommend routing our DPA to your procurement team right after you review the MAP so the first redline pass happens during the security review window.

- Recommended deployment for PHI-limited evaluation: Redwood Dedicated is the usual recommendation for predictable throughput + isolation while keeping procurement and contracting straightforward. Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option but typically adds legal and infra onboarding time.

Next steps I propose: I attached a concise MAP (Aurelia_MAP_v2.pdf) that proposes milestone dates assuming a 3-week close window starting 12/01. Could you confirm whether your internal decision target of 12/20 is fixed? If yes, we will compress DPA turnarounds and ask legal to prioritize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Aurelia_MAP_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial MAP / legal sequencing questions for pilot

Hi Marta / Kim — looping in legal/ops for the sequencing details. Summary of internal constraints from legal ops: 

- MSA: our standard turnaround for a customer redline is 5–10 business days if changes are limited to commercial terms (SOW, pricing, warranty). Anything touching liability caps or indemnity can add 1–2 weeks.
- DPA: we can typically turn the DPA in 3–7 business days if we get the first redline from the customer in the 48-hour window. If Aurelia requires bespoke data residency or additional audit language, expect additional back-and-forth.
- Order form: once SOW/pricing is agreed, order form prep and signature by both sides usually happens within 2 business days.

We will flag this as a priority for the 12/20 decision timeline. Attached are our recommended document templates and a tracked-redline example (DPA_redlines_20261208.docx).

Requested from Aurelia: please share the first DPA redline and confirm whether your procurement needs a PO number before countersignature. That will change the order form timing.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Kim / Vanessa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the MAP. We reviewed the draft and proposed a couple of DPA clarifications in the attached redline; Tom will send the formal redline later tonight. To confirm our constraints:

- 12/20 is our internal target to sign the order form and begin the Dedicated pilot on 01/04. Procurement will try to provide a PO number before countersignature but cannot guarantee it; if the PO lags, we will still sign the order form and provide the PO within 5 business days of signature.
- We accept Dedicated as the recommended environment.

Next actions:
- Tom: share DPA redline (incoming)
- Kimberly/Vanessa/Karthik: legal to review redline within 48 business hours and flag any material liabilities
- Both teams: align on go/no-go criteria in MAP (we updated acceptance criteria to include latency SLA checks during week 2 of evaluation)

Appreciate the coordination — we’ll upload the signed order form to DocuSign as soon as countersigned.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Aurelia Health
